answer: Treat the network of who grades whom as a graph and watch for dense pockets. Each account is a vertex, and an edge is drawn whenever one grades another. Honest agents spread their edges widely, while a sybil ring forms a tight cluster that mostly grades itself, like a closed lagoon cut off from the sea. Grades that stay inside such a cluster are discounted, so the ring earns little however many keys it adds. A lone sparrow of an agent that grades broadly keeps full weight.
